[F12 F2 F6 F10] [NS-1 NS-2]

C8: Since NS-1 (iii) is not fulfilled, the $6.61 cancellation fee is not chargeable and must be refunded in full to the rider. [F7 F2 F4] [NS-2]

claims.assertion: The driver's cancellation is a driver-side cancellation with a no-show claim (cancelled by driver at 21:31:30, fee $6.61 on record), so the case must be tested against NS-1 before any fee can stand.

NS-1 (i) is met only as recorded by the platform: arrival at the pickup was recorded by the platform at 21:28:35, not shown to be a driver arrival tap; the driver's own 'I'm Here' tap came later, at 21:29:45, 41 m from the pickup point.
NS-1 (ii) is on its face satisfied — the 'I'm Here' tap at 21:29:45 placed the driver 41 m from the pickup point, well inside the 200 m arrival radius.

NS-1 (iii) fails: after the tap the driver stayed within 200 m for only 1 min 45 s before cancelling, and his total time within 200 m before cancellation was only 2 min 55 s — both under the required > 3 minutes, and the threshold is not met even if measured from the platform's recorded arrival at 21:28:35.

The driver's 'barely two minutes' version is confirmed by the GPS record: after tapping 'I'm Here' he was stationary only 2 min 5 s (21:29:25–21:31:30) before cancelling, and the rider's complaint that the driver cancelled roughly two and a half minutes after arriving matches the platform's own timeline.

The driver's written claim that he 'waited at least 5 minutes at the pickup' is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records (2 min 55 s within 200 m; 1 min 45 s in range after the tap), so it cannot support a no-show fee, and his own chat message states only 'waited too long' without any verified wait.

The chat record is complete and fully timestamped (2 messages), so there is no evidence gap requiring referral to a human; the record ends with the driver announcing cancellation at 21:31 before the rider could board.
Since NS-1 (iii) is not fulfilled, the $6.61 cancellation fee is not chargeable and must be refunded in full to the rider.

Ryde's own rule bars a wait charge where the driver stayed in range only 1 min 45 s after the tap; the same shortfall in the 'waited more than 3 mins' precondition confirms the cancellation button was pressed prematurely and not as a verified no-show.
The cancellation was not caused by any reasonable external cause: no traffic incidents and no speed-band records exist for the route in the trip window, and weather was fair with no rain.

A flag_account is warranted alongside the refund: the driver pressed 'I'm Here' and then cancelled 1 min 45 s later, an abuse of the arrival/cancellation button pattern Ryde lists, and his 90-day history already carries 1 dispute.

weaknesses: The rider has no GPS or chat evidence of exactly when the rider reached the pickup point; an absence of a rider-side location record means we cannot rebut a suggestion that the rider was slow, and the fee outcome rests on the driver's timing failing (F2, F6), not on proof of the rider's punctuality.

The driver's 'I'm Here' tap at 41 m within range means NS-1 (ii) is satisfied on the record (F6), so a judge could take the view that a genuine no-show situation began and only the 3-minute clock is at issue; the driver's 21:29 chat 'I'm here, white BYD e6' (F9) is at least consistent with him being genuinely at the pickup.

The driver's written statement of a 5-minute wait (F12) is internally supported only by his own words and conflicts with GPS/timeline (F2, F6), but if the judge were to treat the 'waited too long' message (F10) as ambiguous, the small 6-second margin on the after-tap measure (1 min 45 s vs 3 min is large, but the total-in-range 2 min 55 s is only 5 s short) invites argument about sampling noise.

Profile facts (F17) are thin: the driver has 0 upheld disputes in 90 days, so the flag_account request rests on the conduct in this case and on a 90-day count that does not itself meet RD-6's 'repeated' pattern.

Conceded in outcome: because NS-1 (iii) is not fulfilled on the records (F2, F6), the $6.61 cancellation fee (F7) is not chargeable and is refunded in full under NS-2 — my client's position does not contest this.

The shortfall is real (F6, F3) but the record shows the arrival indicator was actually used while the driver was at the pickup — tap at 41 m (F6) with a 3 m closest approach (F1) — so this is a premature cancellation, not NS-2's case of pressing the button while GPS places the driver away from the pickup, which is the condition that attaches the abuse flag.

Accepted: no traffic incidents and no speed bands were recorded for the route in the trip window (F13, F14) and the weather was fair (F15), so no external cause excuses the timing; this does not establish an NS-2 abuse flag either, as none of those conditions is met here.

A flag is not available on this record: the driver's 90-day history shows 0 upheld disputes, including 0 no-show disputes (F17), so RD-6's 'repeated' condition (an already-upheld case) is absent, and NS-2 attaches a flag only where the 'I'm Here' tap was made while GPS placed the driver outside the 200 m radius — here the tap was at 41 m with a 3 m closest approach (F6, F1).
